question: Give two examples of application software used for general office tasks at Lakewood Insurance.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each correct response, up to a maximum of two marks.

Spreadsheet / Microsoft Excel (1)
Email client / Microsoft Outlook (1)
Database software / Microsoft Access (1)
Presentation software / Microsoft PowerPoint (1)

scenario: Maya uses a tablet computer running a mobile operating system for both work and leisure.
question: Explain one difference between a mobile operating system and a desktop operating system.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for identification and one mark for an appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of two marks.
points: A mobile OS is designed to manage battery consumption efficiently (1) whereas a desktop OS assumes a constant mains power supply and does not prioritise battery saving (1)
A mobile OS is optimised for touchscreen input (1) whereas a desktop OS is primarily designed for mouse and keyboard interaction (1)
A mobile OS runs on devices with limited hardware resources (less RAM, lower-power CPU) (1) so it is designed to be lightweight and efficient compared to a full desktop OS (1)

scenario: Harbourne Travel Agency is implementing a new online booking system. Before going live, the IT team must test the system thoroughly.
question: Give two types of testing that Harbourne Travel Agency should carry out before launching the new booking system.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each correct response, up to a maximum of two marks.
points: User acceptance testing (UAT) — testing by end users to confirm the system meets their requirements (1)
Functional testing — verifying each feature works as specified (1)
Performance/load testing — checking the system can handle expected numbers of simultaneous users (1)
Security testing — checking for vulnerabilities in the system (1)
Integration testing — checking the new system works correctly with existing systems (1)

scenario: Kingsway Superstore uses an automatic data processing system at its checkouts where barcode scanners read product codes and automatically update stock levels.
question: Explain one benefit to Kingsway Superstore of using automatic rather than manual data processing at its checkouts.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for identification and one mark for an appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of two marks.
points: Automatic processing is faster than manual data entry (1) allowing checkouts to process customers more quickly and reduce queuing times (1)
Automatic processing eliminates human input errors (1) ensuring stock levels and sales data are accurate without staff needing to type in product codes (1)
Stock records are updated in real time automatically (1) allowing the store to monitor levels and trigger re-orders without manual checking (1)

scenario: Firstly Bank installs ATM machines that use a menu-driven interface for customers to access their account services.
question: Explain one advantage of a menu-driven interface for customers using an ATM machine.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for identification and one mark for an appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of two marks.
points: A menu-driven interface presents a limited set of options at each step (1) making it easy for customers of all ages and IT experience levels to use without any training (1)
The user cannot accidentally enter incorrect commands (1) as they can only select from the predefined options shown on screen (1)
The interface guides users through the transaction process step by step (1) reducing errors and ensuring the correct sequence is followed (1)

topic: A1.2.4 Retail use of digital devices
scenario: Orchard & Vine is an independent wine merchant with an online store and a physical shop in Bristol.
question: Explain one way that a mobile device could be used by staff at Orchard & Vine to improve customer service in the physical shop.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for identification and one mark for an appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of two marks.
points: Staff can use a tablet to access product information and stock levels in real time (1) allowing them to answer customer queries accurately without leaving the shop floor (1)
A tablet with a card reader attachment can process payments anywhere in the shop (1) removing the need for customers to queue at a fixed till and improving the shopping experience (1)
Staff can use a mobile device to access customer order history (1) allowing them to make personalised wine recommendations based on previous purchases (1)

scenario: Thornfield Academy is reviewing the storage devices used across its network for student and staff data.
question: Describe two different types of storage device and explain a use of each at Thornfield Academy.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark per device description and one mark for its use, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Hard disk drive (HDD) (1) — used as the main storage in the school's file server to store all student coursework, staff files and curriculum resources due to high capacity and low cost (1)
Solid state drive (SSD) (1) — installed in student laptops to store the OS and applications, providing fast boot times and quick file access during lessons (1)
USB flash drive / memory stick (1) — used by students to carry work between school and home or to submit coursework digitally (1)
Network attached storage (NAS) (1) — used to provide centralised, shared storage accessible from all computers on the school network (1)
Optical disc / DVD (1) — used to distribute software or archive historical records (1)

scenario: Meridian Bank processes millions of customer transactions daily. Its IT security team relies on the operating system to enforce security policies across all bank computers.
question: Explain two security functions performed by the operating system at Meridian Bank.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each identification and one mark for each appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Access control (1) — the OS requires all users to authenticate with a username and password (or MFA) before they can log in, preventing unauthorised individuals from accessing the bank's systems (1)
Firewall management (1) — the OS can enforce firewall rules to filter network traffic, blocking unauthorised incoming or outgoing connections that could expose banking data (1)
Encryption (1) — the OS can encrypt files stored on disk, ensuring that even if physical media is stolen, customer financial data cannot be read (1)
Malware protection (1) — the OS monitors running processes and can quarantine or block software that behaves maliciously (1)
Audit logging (1) — the OS records all user actions and access events, creating an audit trail that allows the security team to investigate any suspicious activity (1)

scenario: Highfield Veterinary Practice is purchasing new computer equipment for its consulting rooms and reception area. The practice manager needs to ensure all devices can connect to each other and to the internet.
question: Explain two connectivity factors that Highfield Veterinary Practice should consider when choosing its new IT equipment.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each identification and one mark for each appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Wi-Fi capability (1) — consulting room computers must be able to connect wirelessly to the practice network so that vets can access patient records without cables running across the floor, which would be a tripping hazard (1)
USB and peripheral ports (1) — computers need appropriate ports to connect printers, card readers and diagnostic equipment such as digital X-ray systems (1)
Network interface card / Ethernet port (1) — a wired connection for the reception computer would provide faster and more reliable internet access for processing online booking and payment systems (1)
Bluetooth connectivity (1) — allows wireless connection of peripherals such as printers or card readers without cables cluttering the consulting rooms (1)

scenario: Rosewood Hotels Group equips each of its guest rooms with a smart entertainment system. Guests can stream films, browse the internet and control room settings from a single device.
question: Describe two features of a smart entertainment system and explain how each benefits hotel guests.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark per feature and one mark for a linked benefit, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Video streaming capability (1) — guests can watch films and TV programmes on demand from services such as Netflix, removing the need for a traditional TV schedule and improving guest satisfaction (1)
Internet browsing (1) — guests can access travel information, maps and email from the comfort of their room, making their stay more convenient (1)
Smart room controls / IoT integration (1) — guests can adjust lighting, temperature and curtains from one device, providing a personalised and convenient experience (1)
Wireless connectivity via Wi-Fi (1) — guests can connect their own devices to the system without cables, providing a seamless experience (1)

topic: A3.4.4 Features; A3.4.5 Business and user needs — software choice
scenario: Bluebell Care Home manages the welfare of 60 elderly residents. The manager is choosing specialist care home management software to replace a paper-based system.
question: Explain two business or user needs that Bluebell Care Home should consider when choosing care management software.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each identification and one mark for each appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Ease of use for care staff (1) — care workers are not IT specialists, so the software must have an intuitive interface that does not require extensive training to use effectively during a busy working day (1)
Regulatory compliance features (1) — care homes are subject to CQC regulations; the software must support creation of care plans, medication records and incident reports in a compliant format (1)
Data security and access control (1) — resident health data is highly sensitive and must be protected; the software must restrict access to authorised staff only (1)
Compatibility with GP and NHS systems (1) — the software should be able to share data with external healthcare providers to ensure continuity of care for residents (1)
Mobile access (1) — care staff often work across different rooms and should be able to update records on a tablet or mobile device at the point of care (1)

scenario: Fortuna Architects stores large CAD files, 3D renders and project archives. The firm has a tight IT budget and is comparing different storage options.
question: Describe how cost affects the choice of storage media for Fortuna Architects, with reference to two different storage types.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark per storage type and one mark for a linked cost consideration, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: Hard disk drives (HDDs) have a lower cost per gigabyte than SSDs (1) making them a cost-effective choice for storing large CAD archives where speed is less critical than capacity (1)
Solid state drives (SSDs) are significantly more expensive per gigabyte than HDDs (1) but their speed benefit may justify the cost for the firm's active project files that are accessed frequently (1)
Cloud storage involves a recurring monthly subscription cost (1) which may be affordable but accumulates over time, potentially exceeding the one-off cost of physical storage (1)
Tape storage has a very low cost per gigabyte (1) making it economical for long-term archiving of completed project files that rarely need to be accessed (1)

scenario: Broadlands NHS Trust is choosing a new electronic prescribing system. The trust processes over 5,000 prescriptions per day across its wards.
question: Explain two ways in which efficiency should influence the choice of electronic prescribing system at Broadlands NHS Trust.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each identification and one mark for each appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: The system must process prescriptions quickly (1) as with 5,000 prescriptions per day, a slow system would create dangerous delays in patients receiving medication (1)

The interface must allow prescribers to complete a prescription with minimal steps (1) saving time for busy doctors and nurses who could otherwise spend excessive time on data entry instead of patient care (1)
The system should integrate with pharmacy dispensing software (1) automating the transfer of prescriptions and eliminating the need for pharmacists to re-enter data manually (1)
Efficient search and autocomplete features for medication names (1) reduce the time taken to prescribe and help avoid errors caused by typing drug names incorrectly (1)

scenario: Kiosks at Heathrow Airport provide passengers with flight information and allow them to print boarding passes. Each kiosk runs a dedicated single-use operating system.
question: Describe two features of a single-use operating system and explain why it is suitable for the airport kiosks.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark per feature and one mark for a linked justification, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: A single-use OS is designed to run only one specific application (1) which is appropriate for the kiosks as passengers only need to use the boarding pass and flight information application — no other software is needed (1)
A single-use OS is lightweight and requires minimal hardware resources (1) making it reliable and fast for the specific task while reducing the cost of kiosk hardware (1)
A single-use OS reduces the attack surface for cybersecurity threats (1) as there are no unnecessary applications or services running that could be exploited by malicious actors (1)
A single-use OS boots directly into the required application (1) meaning kiosks are available immediately for passengers without any complex startup processes (1)

scenario: Streamline Productions is a video production company. Its video editors use computers to edit 4K footage. The technical director is writing the hardware specification for new editing workstations.
question: Explain two hardware specifications that are most important when choosing computers for 4K video editing at Streamline Productions.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for each identification and one mark for each appropriate linked justification/expansion, up to a maximum of four marks.
points: High-capacity fast storage / NVMe SSD (1) — 4K footage files are very large, so fast storage allows the editor to load and scrub through footage without buffering or lag (1)
Powerful multi-core CPU (1) — video encoding and real-time preview rendering of 4K footage requires significant processing power; a high-core-count CPU reduces render time (1)
Dedicated GPU with large VRAM (1) — GPU-accelerated video editing software offloads rendering to the GPU, dramatically speeding up preview and export of 4K content (1)

Large RAM (32–64 GB or more) (1) — video editing software loads large portions of footage into RAM; insufficient RAM causes the system to use slower virtual memory, significantly degrading performance (1)

scenario: Apex Customer Services is a call centre that handles enquiries and complaints for several retail clients. The company is piloting an AI chatbot to handle routine customer queries automatically, alongside human agents who manage complex issues.
question: Explain one implication for Apex Customer Services of introducing an AI chatbot to handle routine customer queries.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award one mark for identification, one mark for linked justification, and one mark for further expansion, up to a maximum of three marks.
points: The chatbot can handle queries 24 hours a day without breaks (1) improving service availability outside normal call centre hours (1) which is a significant benefit for customers of retail clients who shop at evenings and weekends (1)

Human call centre agents are freed from routine queries (1) allowing them to focus their time on complex or sensitive issues requiring empathy and judgement (1) improving overall service quality and potentially reducing staffing costs for routine handling (1)

If the chatbot is not trained on a sufficient range of queries it may give incorrect or unhelpful responses (1) frustrating customers who then still need to be transferred to a human agent (1) potentially damaging the reputation of Apex and its retail clients (1)
